comments.body:
RCA CONFIRMED + REPAIR EVIDENCE (rebar-debug run)

## Measurements re-verified at origin/main (3834269c53)

F1 applier/invariants: `applier.py` yields 0 matches for the guard's three line prefixes.
    DOUBLY vacuous — the facade imports siblings as `from rebar_reconciler.<mod> import ...`,
    a spelling NONE of the three prefixes (`from .invariants`, `from invariants`,
    `import invariants`) can match, so even an invariants import placed in applier.py itself
    was invisible. The AC's subject, `inbound_repair_property`, lives in `apply_inbound.py`.
    All "invariants" hits across the apply* family are docstrings/comments; 0 real imports.
F2 llm wall-clock: `signal.alarm`/`Timer(` measured 0 across ALL of `src/rebar/` — the scan
    of `runner.py` alone had no denominator; timeout machinery sits in `structured_run.py`
    and `agent_call.py`.
F3 probe neutrality: `inbound_probe.py` has 0 rebar imports of any kind.
F4 usage-log colon split: `usage_log.py` has 0 banned string-parse calls. `_pricing_model_ref`
    still happens to live there, so this one was aimed correctly but had no anti-vacuity
    assertion — the next relocation disarms it exactly as F1-F3 were disarmed.

## Repairs (test-only; no production behaviour changed)

Each guard now DERIVES its scan population instead of pinning a filename, gains an
anti-vacuity assertion on that population, and gains a teeth test driven through REAL
modules (not just a synthetic string — a synthetic-source test proves the predicate works
but cannot detect the guard being aimed at the wrong file, which is how all four survived).

F1 -> applier facade + transitive closure of its intra-package imports; AST import scan
      replaces line-prefix matching (catches the absolute spelling). Landmark: the
      population must define `inbound_repair_property`.
F2 -> runner + transitive closure of its intra-`rebar.llm` imports. Landmark: >= 2 scanned
      modules must mention a timeout.
F3 -> `inbound_probe` + transitive closure of its intra-package imports. Landmark: the
      population must define `ProbeBranch` and `ProbeConfigError`.
F4 -> population DERIVED from where `_pricing_model_ref`/`_price_row` are DEFINED (a
      package glob was rejected: the wider `rebar.llm` package legitimately parses ':' in
      provider registries and capability tables, and a guard that fires on those gets
      deleted). `config.split_provider_qualifier` stays the sanctioned delegate.
F6 -> relative `pathlib.Path("src/rebar/...")` anchored to the imported module's `__file__`.
      Proven: the old literal raises FileNotFoundError when pytest runs from any cwd but the
      repo root; the guard now passes from `/tmp`.

## Mutation checks (plant violation -> RED, remove -> GREEN). ALL FOUR PASS.

F1: planted `from rebar_reconciler.invariants import check_schema` in `apply_inbound.py`
    -> NEW guard RED (`apply_inbound:1`); OLD pinned guard GREEN (vacuous). Restored: GREEN.
F2: planted a `Timer(` in `structured_run.py` -> NEW RED (`structured_run: Timer(`);
    OLD GREEN (vacuous). Restored: GREEN.
F3: split the vocabulary into a new `probe_vocab.py` importing `adapters.jira`
    -> NEW RED (2 offenders); OLD GREEN (vacuous). Restored: GREEN.
F4: relocated `_pricing_model_ref` into a sibling `pricing_ref.py` that colon-splits
    -> NEW RED (`pricing_ref:3`); OLD GREEN (vacuous). Restored: GREEN.

## Dispositions for the remaining findings

F5 (`test_bedrock_provider.py`, capabilities.py prefix-matching) — FIXED, lightly. The
   module still holds the exact-id tables, so the guard is aimed correctly; it lacked the
   anti-vacuity assertion. Added a landmark requiring `_REBAR_OVERRIDES` and
   `_MODEL_ID_CAPABILITY_OVERRIDES` to still be defined in the scanned module.

F7 (`test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py` 4-file list vs `adapters/jira/backend.py`) —
   ACCEPTED, with reason. `backend.py`'s `set_relationship` (:217) and `add_comment` (:271)
   are ONE-LINE pure delegations to `self.transport.<same name>(...)`, explicitly sectioned
   "delegates to transport". They issue no HTTP call and therefore carry no 429 policy of
   their own; the rate-limit sweep is correctly scoped to the transport modules. NOT a
   vacuity bug. The residual fragility is real but different in kind — the hardcoded list
   would miss a NEW transport module — and closing it requires classifying every member of
   the whole `adapters/jira/` package as mutating/non-mutating, which is a judgement task,
   not a mechanical one. Filed as follow-up rather than forced into this bug.

F8 (`test_container_roster.py` vs `plan_review/passes.py:403`) — ACCEPTED: FALSE POSITIVE of
   the original sweep. `passes.py:403` renders per-child PROMPT SECTIONS
   (`### child <id>: <title>\n<description>`) and `det_floor.py:633` estimates TOKENS for a
   parent+child pairing. Neither is the sibling roster (`- <id>: <title>`), and both already
   carry descriptions — so neither exhibits the title-only defect the guard exists to
   prevent. They merely share a substring with it.

compiled_state.description:
Discovered by the Step-7 sibling sweep of bug 34c2 (DC pagination guard went vacuous after
465d's module split). Same defect class: a structural test pins its `ast.parse` /
`inspect.getsource` scan to ONE hardcoded source file, a later refactor moves the policed
construct into a sibling module, and the guard silently starts passing unconditionally.

Each finding below was MEASURED (occurrence count in the scanned target), not suspected.

## Confirmed vacuous (zero instances of the policed construct in the scanned target)

1. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_applier_repair_property.py:24,136`
   Scans `rebar_reconciler/applier.py` only, for `import invariants`. `applier.py` is now a
   pure re-export facade; the function the AC is actually about, `_repair_property`, lives in
   `apply_inbound.py` — which even carries the AC text verbatim at `apply_inbound.py:294-295`
   and is NOT scanned. Measured: 0 matching imports in the scanned file.

2. `tests/unit/test_llm_timeouts.py:335-336`
   `inspect.getsource(rebar.llm.runner)`, looking for `signal.alarm` / `Timer(`. The
   timeout-bearing code was split out into `llm/structured_run.py` (7 `timeout` refs) and
   `llm/agent_call.py` (3); `runner.py` now names `timeout` once. Measured: 0/0 in the
   scanned module. A new wall-clock primitive would land in the unscanned half.

3. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/fetch/test_probe_capability_heldout.py:62`
   Scans `inbound_probe.py` for imports naming `adapters.jira` / `acli_subprocess`.
   `inbound_probe.py` is now a 55-line pure-vocabulary module whose only imports are
   stdlib; its own docstring says the mechanics live in `adapters/jira/probe.py` (unscanned,
   alongside `adapters/jira_family/probe.py`). Measured: 0 rebar imports of any kind —
   structurally impossible to fail.

4. `tests/unit/test_usage_log_pricing_qualified_2ca9.py:118`
   Scans `llm/usage_log.py` for `.split/.partition/.startswith(...)` taking a `":"`
   argument. Measured: 596 LOC containing ZERO string-parsing method calls of any kind, so
   the predicate has no denominator. The actual splitting lives in
   `config.split_provider_qualifier` (unscanned).

## Borderline — empty population today, so unfallable in practice

5. `tests/unit/test_bedrock_provider.py:119` — scans `llm/capabilities.py` (669 LOC) for
   `.startswith`/`.endswith`; measured 0. Still the plausible home for model-id tables, but
   nothing pins that, unlike finding 8 below.
6. `tests/unit/test_code_review_assemble.py:88-92` — scans
   `llm/code_review/assemble.py` for forbidden intra-package imports; measured 0 of any
   kind. Separately, its path is RELATIVE (`pathlib.Path("src/rebar/...")`) rather than
   anchored to `__file__` — the only guard in the audit that breaks if cwd is not the repo
   root.

## Non-vacuous but leaking outside a hardcoded scan list (at-risk, same shape)

7. `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/test_cloud_rate_limit_sweep_heldout.py:511-514` enumerates
   mutating members across a hardcoded 4-file list under `adapters/jira/`; `adapters/jira/
   backend.py` (unscanned) already defines `add_comment` and `set_relationship`.
8. `tests/unit/test_container_roster.py:103-118` forbids an inline roster literal in two
   modules; that literal still exists once in `plan_review/passes.py` (unscanned).

## The fix pattern (already proven on 34c2)

The single distinguishing feature of every guard that SURVIVED a relocation is an explicit
anti-vacuity/coverage assertion — see `test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py:630` ("the whole
guard is VACUOUS" if the readers move) and `test_web_tool_gating.py:130`. None of findings
1-6 has one. 34c2 fixed its guard by (a) widening the scan from one file to the package and
(b) adding `test_the_guard_scans_the_modules_that_hold_the_calls`, which asserts the scan
POPULATION covers every module actually holding the construct. Apply the same two moves here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Findings 1-4 each either re-targeted to where the construct now lives, or deleted with
      a recorded rationale; verified by `pytest` going RED when the construct is
      synthetically re-introduced at its real home
- [ ] Each repaired guard gains an anti-vacuity assertion proving its scan population is
      non-empty (the pattern from `test_acli_graph_pagination_heldout.py:630`)
- [ ] Finding 6's relative path anchored to `__file__`
- [ ] Findings 5, 7, 8 explicitly dispositioned (fix or accept-with-reason)

## Testing

- `.venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/unit tests/interfaces -q` stays green
- For each repaired guard: mutation check — re-introduce the policed construct at its real
  current home and confirm the guard goes RED (proving it is no longer vacuous)
